title: Implement structured log ingestion pipeline for Loki with correlation IDs and parsing schema
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a robust, cost-effective structured log ingestion and aggregation pipeline that attaches correlation IDs to logs, normalizes JSON fields, and pushes into Grafana Loki for low-cost query/alerting. Scope includes: (1) runtime tracing hooks to emit trace_id/request_id from Redwood services, (2) an ingestion pipeline (Promtail/Vector -> Kafka buffering -> Loki distributors/ingesters) with structured parsing and schema enforcement, (3) parsing rules and label design to enable high-cardinality queries for latency/error dashboards, and (4) rollout + migration strategy for existing unstructured logs.

Design decisions and rationale:
- Backend choice: Loki chosen for primary ingestion because label-based indexing and chunk storage keeps costs predictable for high-volume ephemeral inference logs. We will keep an option to forward sampled, enriched, full-text logs to Elasticsearch for deep text search or forensic needs.
- Pipeline components: Promtail/Vector as forwarders for structured JSON; Vector preferred for CPU and memory efficiency and its transformation primitives (remap) — but we will keep Promtail as a fall-back for edge clusters. Kafka (or Kinesis in specific AWS regions) will be used as a durable buffer between forwarders and Loki distributors to absorb bursts and allow backpressure handling.
- Schema: Define a minimal semantic log schema to be enforced at ingestion: timestamp_iso, service, env, level, message, request_id, trace_id, span_id, span_parent_id, latency_ms, status_code, error_type, error_stack (redacted), user_id_hash (PII hashed), model_id, model_version, shard_id, node_id. Fields not in schema allowed in a free-form attributes object but not indexed as labels.
- Correlation IDs: Runtime tracing hooks (see attachments) will ensure every incoming external request generates/propagates request_id and trace_id via headers (X-Request-Id, X-Trace-Id). Language SDKs and server middleware (Go/Python/Java) must write these IDs into structured logs and into OpenTelemetry spans.
- Label strategy for Loki: Small set of cardinality-controlled labels for queries: service, env, level, model_id, model_version, request_id, trace_id (only for tracing joins), status_code_bucket (2xx/4xx/5xx), shard_id. Avoid making user_id or arbitrary attributes labels.
- Parsing: Use Vector/Promtail harvest + remap to parse JSON fields, coerce types (latency_ms -> integer), validate presence of trace_id/request_id for high-priority services, and emit parsing_error metrics when malformed.
- Retention and cost: Raw chunks in Loki retained 14 days by default; processed, sampled exports to ES/S3 for 90+ day retention. Compression and chunk limits configured to balance memory footprint.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Ingestion pipeline demonstrates stable throughput of 3GB/s peak per region with <0.5% dropped logs across a 24h soak test.
- Trace_id/request_id appears on 99% of logs for instrumented services after rollout.
- Parsing error rate <0.1% for structured JSON logs.
- Dashboards (latency + error) show correct comparisons to tracing-derived spans and support drill-down from aggregated anomalies to raw log lines.

Rollout plan and migration:
1) Prototype: small cluster ingest from staging services with Vector -> Kafka -> Loki. Validate schema, metrics, and cost. (Done: prototype cluster up, see attachments.)
2) Libraries/middleware: ship tracing hooks and log middleware for Go (zap), Python (structlog/structlog-ext), and Java (logback) with standard keys and a helper to redact PII. Deliver as internal SDKs.
3) Gradual enablement: enable structured logging in low-traffic services, run two-week soak, then enable in core runtime. Provide fallbacks to unstructured parsing with sampling during transition.
4) Backfill: For critical timelines we will run on-demand ingestion jobs to parse historic logs into the new schema for top services only.

Security and compliance:
- PII must be redacted at edge (forwarders) or hashed using salted HMAC before reaching Kafka.
- Sensitive fields (error_stack) will be encrypted at rest when stored long-term and access-controlled via Grafana/ACLs.
- Ensure log exporters authenticate with mutual TLS and use KMS for key management.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- Metrics to emit: logs_ingest_bytes_total, logs_ingest_errors_total, logs_dropped_total, parsing_errors_total, logs_kafka_lag_seconds, loki_chunk_write_errors_total.
- Alerts: parsing_errors_total > 0.1% sustained for 10m, logs_dropped_total > 100/min, kafka_lag > threshold for 5m.

Open trade-offs and follow-ups:
- Loki vs ES: Loki lowers cost for our high-volume telemetry but makes free-text queries harder. We recommend a hybrid strategy for investigatory workflows.
- Labels cardinality: Ensure teams do not migrate arbitrary identifiers into labels. We'll ship validation tooling to catch this.
- Sampling: Consider server-side adaptive sampling for verbose debug logs to control costs (future work).

Next steps (short term):
- Finalize Vector configuration and remap rules (owner: Evan).
- Deliver SDK middleware PRs for Go/Python/Java (PRs referenced below).
- Run 72-hour soak in staging and provide cost projection.
- Security review and compliance sign-off before enabling in production.

qa_notes: Run staging soak: 72h, 2 rollups: 1) structured JSON only, 2) mixed structured+unstructured. Validate trace_id propagation by sampling 10k traces and confirming log joins. Verify throttling behavior by simulating 2x usual traffic.
risk_summary: Medium risk: schema enforcement may temporarily drop or mis-label logs during rollout. Mitigations: sampling, fallback parsing, and alerting on parsing_errors_total. Cost risk if retention or labels are misconfigured; include cost cap in initial rollout.
